notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Identity and knowledge are delivered foundations, not a fleet implementation. Durable assignments, addressed inboxes/acknowledgements, atomic task/thread/inbox handoff and exact-revision review coverage remain new work. Preserve the owner decision to finish remote commit verification before autonomous fleet execution; no new launcher or coordination implementation is selected here.

problem: Shared memory alone does not tell cooperating agents who owns a task, whether a question was received, or which revision a review verified.
Interrupted sessions, overlapping scope, and repeated full-context reads make multi-agent work hard to continue and supervise.

risk.rollback: Keep coordination additive to memory and runtime services. Disable coordination entry points while preserving assignments, messages, handoffs, and exports; do not alter runtime claims or terminate independent agent processes.

scope: Follow docs/agent-fleet-coordination-plan.md after the basic shared memory and identity services; split bounded implementation slices before coding.
Separate durable agent identities from execution sessions, and task assignments from server claims. Use atomic transitions, revision checks, expiry visibility, and explicit reassignment.
Add addressed messages with distinct delivery and acknowledgement states, authorized subscriptions, and bounded changes-since reads with visible resync behavior.
Record interruption/completion handoffs and review/test evidence for exact source revisions. Surface blockers, last contact, and pending owner decisions.

Keep session launch, wakeup, enforced cancellation, concurrency budgets, and measured spend behind later explicitly supported runner adapters. Do not promise control over external agents or infer costs.

Implement handoff as a revision-checked, retry-safe transaction linking a task offer, forum message, and recipient inbox. Keep named recipients distinct from role queues; provide explicit acceptance, decline, and questions through shared UI/MCP/CLI semantics. Start with owner-selected specialist profiles and source-linked contract/evidence context.
title: Coordinate agent assignments, messages, handoffs, and owner oversight
validation: Fixtures cover concurrent task acquisition, stale assignment writes, expiry, reassignment, identity revocation, and preserved partial work.
Verify message retries, reconnects, explicit acknowledgements, authorization, bounded pagination, and expired-cursor recovery without silently losing events.
Prove an owner-directed three-agent implementation/review/investigation workflow with actual client sessions; label fixture-only evidence separately.
Changing the reviewed revision exposes stale review coverage. Missing runner or cost instrumentation appears as unavailable rather than confirmed execution state or measured spend.
Coordination reads/writes neither acquire runtime claims nor start or stop managed servers. Export and restart preserve durable coordination history.

Verify atomic task/thread/inbox creation, duplicate retries, acceptance versus acknowledgement, stale/cancelled offers, unauthorized recipients, and competing role acceptors. Offline offers remain discoverable without a launcher. Specialist handover retains API contract versions and checks the integrated result rather than assuming separate component success is sufficient.
value: Humans and multiple agents can coordinate work without losing questions, partial results, or the provenance of verification.
The owner can distinguish blocked work, unknown session state, and results needing review before considering automated fleet execution.
